_comment: Species reference data. This is the file you edit to add an animal.
To add one: drop <key>.raw.png into this directory, run
scripts/prep_silhouettes.py, and add an entry here whose key matches
the filename. No Rust or JavaScript changes are needed.
Dimensions are typical adult figures gathered from hunting and
wildlife references. They are approximations - real animals vary a
lot by region, subspecies, age and condition - so the app lets the
user override body_length_in and shoulder_height_in at runtime.
Treat these as starting points, not authoritative measurements.
vitals_anchor is where the heart/lung centre sits within the trimmed
artwork, as a fraction of its width and height (0,0 = top-left).
It is eyeballed against each silhouette.

roe.habitat: Woodland edges, farmland and scrub across Europe; browses in the open at dawn and dusk.
roe.diet: Herbivore: buds, shoots, leaves, herbs, brambles and farm crops.
fun_facts: Small and light for a deer - a mature buck often weighs under 70 lb, so the vital zone is correspondingly tight.
Bucks shed and regrow antlers over winter, opposite to most deer, which regrow them in spring and summer.

phallow.habitat: Mature broadleaf woodland with open grazing nearby; widely introduced well beyond its native range.
phallow.diet: Herbivore: grasses, herbs, browse, acorns and other mast.
fun_facts: The only deer with broad, flattened palmate antlers apart from moose.
Coats vary enormously between individuals, from near-white to almost black, in the same population.

elk.habitat: Mountain meadows, foothills and open forest; moves to lower elevations in winter.
elk.diet: Herbivore: grasses in summer, shifting to woody browse and bark in winter.
fun_facts: Much larger than they photograph - a bull can exceed 700 lb, and the vital zone is roughly the size of a basketball.
Bulls bugle during the rut, a call that carries for miles and is audible well beyond visual range.

moose.habitat: Boreal forest, willow flats, lakeshores and marshy ground across northern latitudes.
moose.diet: Herbivore: willow, birch and aquatic plants; wades and dives to feed.
fun_facts: The largest deer alive - a big bull stands taller at the shoulder than most people.
Despite the bulk they swim strongly and can stay submerged for well over a minute while feeding.

hog.habitat: Highly adaptable: bottomland hardwood forest, marsh, swamp and farmland, usually near water and dense cover.
hog.diet: Omnivore and opportunistic feeder: grasses and forbs in spring, fruit in summer and autumn, roots, tubers and invertebrates year-round.
fun_facts: Can run up to 30 mph despite their bulky build, and are strong swimmers.
Highly intelligent - by some measures on par with or smarter than dogs.
Vitals sit lower and further forward than a deer's, and mature boars grow a thick cartilage shield over the shoulder that can blunt a broadside shot, so quartering-away shots are more reliable.

fox.habitat: Almost anywhere: farmland, woodland, moorland and dense urban areas.
fox.diet: Omnivore: rodents, rabbits, birds, insects, fruit and scavenged food.
fun_facts: The vital zone is only a few inches across, so the margin for error is far smaller than on any deer.
That famously bushy tail is roughly a third of the animal's total length, which makes silhouettes look bigger than the body really is.

pigeon.habitat: Farmland, woodland and towns; feeds in flocks on open fields.
pigeon.diet: Herbivore: seeds, grain, buds, shoots and berries.
fun_facts: A tiny vital zone measured in single-digit inches - this is a shotgun quarry, and the overlay makes that obvious at any real range.
Strong, fast fliers that can sustain well over 50 mph.

turkey.habitat: Open hardwood and mixed forest with clearings; roosts in trees overnight.
turkey.diet: Omnivore: acorns, seeds, greens and insects.
fun_facts: Body mass is mostly feather - the actual vital area is small, which is why head and neck shots are the usual advice.
Can run around 25 mph and fly in short bursts far faster than their bulk suggests.
